column5: The implementation of GHG reduction targets can reinforce the development and use of renewable energy sources, as reducing emissions can create a more favorable environment for renewable energy growth.
Reducing GHG emissions can also reinforce energy efficiency efforts, as energy savings can be achieved through the use of renewable energy sources and energy-efficient technologies.

The reduction of GHG emissions can also lead to the development of new energy infrastructure, such as renewable energy plants and energy storage facilities, which can support the transition to a low-carbon economy.
The growth of renewable energy can enable energy efficiency measures, such as smart grids and energy storage, which can optimize energy distribution and reduce energy waste.

The expansion of renewable energy can drive the development of new energy infrastructure, including transmission and distribution networks, to support the integration of variable renewable energy sources.
The increased use of renewable energy can lead to job creation in the energy sector, contributing to social security and reducing energy poverty.
The development of renewable heating and cooling solutions can reinforce energy efficiency efforts in buildings, reducing energy consumption and greenhouse gas emissions.
The production of renewable hydrogen can support the transition to net-zero emissions in road transport, enabling the use of fuel-cell vehicles and reducing dependence on fossil fuels.
The development of offshore renewable energy can support the decarbonization of maritime transport, reducing emissions from shipping and increasing the use of low-carbon fuels.
The growth of solar energy can enable energy efficiency measures, such as building-integrated photovoltaics and solar water heaters, which can reduce energy consumption and greenhouse gas emissions.
Energy efficiency measures, such as building insulation and efficient lighting, can significantly reduce energy consumption in buildings, supporting the achievement of energy efficiency targets.
Energy-efficient buildings can contribute to social security by reducing energy poverty and improving the health and wellbeing of building occupants.

The development of energy infrastructure, including charging points and hydrogen refueling stations, can support the transition to net-zero emissions in road transport, enabling the use of electric and hydrogen fuel-cell vehicles.

Social security policies, such as those addressing energy poverty, can support the transition to a low-carbon economy by ensuring that the benefits of renewable energy and energy efficiency are shared fairly and that no one is left behind.

The development of rail transport can support the transition to net-zero emissions in road transport, enabling the use of electric and hydrogen fuel-cell vehicles and reducing emissions from freight transport.

The transition to net-zero emissions in road transport can be supported by the use of biofuels, which can provide a low-carbon alternative to fossil fuels and support the achievement of renewable energy targets.

The development of net-zero technology in road transport can be supported by the use of other low-carbon fuels, such as renewable natural gas and methanol, which can reduce emissions and support the achievement of renewable energy targets.

The transition to net-zero emissions in road transport can be supported by the development of hydrogen distribution infrastructure, enabling the use of hydrogen fuel-cell vehicles and reducing dependence on fossil fuels.
Urban mobility solutions, such as electric and hybrid vehicles, can support the transition to a low-carbon economy by reducing emissions from transport and increasing the use of low-carbon fuels.
The use of biofuels in transport logistics can support the achievement of renewable energy targets and reduce emissions from freight transport.
